sentences.text:
In the summer of 1997, hydrophones
picked up *an unprecedented deep ocean anomaly*.
sentences.spoken: In the summer of nineteen ninety-seven, an underwater listening network picked up an anomaly that stunned marine acousticians.

sentences.text:
The Navy had installed the *SOSUS array*
to track submarines through deep ocean channels.
sentences.spoken: The US Navy had installed the SOSUS hydrophone array to track Soviet submarines through the deep sound channel.

sentences.text:
Deep in the South Pacific, an ultra-low sound
echoed across *5,000 kilometers* of water.
sentences.spoken: Deep in the remote South Pacific, a thunderous ultra-low frequency sound echoed across more than five thousand kilometers of open water.

sentences.text:
Named *The Bloop*, the signal rose for
4.5 minutes across multiple stations.
sentences.spoken: Named The Bloop, the signal rose rapidly in frequency over four and a half minutes and was detected by multiple listening stations.

sentences.text:
The acoustic profile looked biological,
yet *several times louder than a Blue Whale*.
sentences.spoken: Its acoustic profile closely resembled an organic biological vocalization, but it was several times louder than the largest blue whale.

sentences.text:
If produced by a creature, it would have to
*measure over 200 feet in length*.
sentences.spoken: Biologists calculated that if an animal produced the sound, it would have to measure well over two hundred feet in length.

sentences.text:
In 2012, NOAA cracked the case:
an *immense Antarctic icequake* cracking glaciers.
sentences.spoken: Finally, in two thousand twelve, NOAA scientists identified the true culprit: an immense icequake caused by massive Antarctic icebergs cracking and calving.

sentences.text:
Shearing ice sheets generated shockwaves
*loud enough to shake an ocean hemisphere*.
sentences.spoken: The shearing of giant ice sheets generated acoustic shockwaves loud enough to shake the entire southern hemisphere.

sentences.text:
Yet 80% of our oceans remain unmapped.
*What else is singing in the dark?*
sentences.spoken: Yet eighty percent of our oceans remain unmapped and unmonitored. What else is singing in the dark?
